name: Datum Sim
tagline: Model and simulate dynamic systems: block diagrams, control and motors.
for: Control, mechanical, electrical, process and mechatronics engineers, researchers and students.
about: Datum Sim models and simulates dynamic systems. You draw the system as blocks and wires: sources, transfer functions, state space, continuous and discrete PID controllers, lookup tables, and a motor library with DC, induction, synchronous, switched reluctance, BLDC and stepper motors, inverters and transforms. Group blocks into subsystems, give them parameters of their own with a mask, and keep them in your own library. Then press Run and watch the signals on live scopes.

Five solvers cover everything from simple fixed-step runs to stiff systems; the variable-step solvers find switching times exactly. Discrete controllers run at their own sample times, and the diagram can colour every block by its rate. Motors come with typical values for low, medium and high voltage ratings. Scopes have measuring cursors, step-response marks and comparison of earlier runs, and a probe reads any wire after a run. Parameter sweeps run in the app's own engine, step-response specifications and Bode plots come from a built-in Python engine, and the solvers, main blocks and motors are checked against known answers.

steps.title: Draw the model
steps.text: Drag blocks, motors and your own saved blocks from the library, wire them together and set their parameters, or pick a typical rating. Name signals, add notes and colour the blocks.

steps.title: Run
steps.text: Choose a solver and a stop time, press Run and watch the scopes live.

steps.title: Analyse and tune
steps.text: Measure with cursors and step-response marks, compare runs, read any wire with the probe, and sweep parameters to tune the controller.

highlights: Draw a model as blocks and wires, press Run and watch live scopes
Scopes with two measuring cursors, step-response marks, comparison of the last five runs, stacked plots, and PNG or SVG pictures
A signal probe: hover any wire after a run to read its value
Wires that route themselves: move segments, branch from a wire, name signals; notes, block colours and Find on the diagram
84 blocks: sources, math, transfer functions, state space, PID, delays, discontinuities, lookup tables, discrete control, motors and drives
Discrete control: discrete transfer function, state space, integrator and PID, rate transition, and sample-time colours on the diagram

Motor library: DC (separately excited, shunt, series, compound), induction (squirrel-cage, double-cage, wound-rotor), synchronous (permanent-magnet, reluctance, wound-field with dampers), switched reluctance, BLDC and stepper
Typical ratings for low, medium and high voltage motors, filled in with one choice
Drives: three-phase source, inverter (average or switched), DC link, PWM, Clarke and Park transforms, encoder, current sensor
Subsystems with masks (parameters of their own, help and typical ratings), My blocks for your own library, and Goto/From tags to send signals without wires
Five solvers, from fixed-step Euler to variable-step and stiff; the variable-step solvers find switching times exactly
Parameter sweeps, plus step-response specifications and Bode plots from the built-in Python engine
The solvers, main blocks and motors checked against known answers, including power balance for the induction, synchronous, DC and BLDC motors
